title: The Boulder That Wouldn't Stay One
story: In the echoing gorge below Thistlecrag, a rolling stone monster blocks the only rescue path to trapped shepherds. Every time it is struck, Knurlvex cracks into 4 rolling boulders — and each of those splits into 4 more if struck again. Mr 6 taps it once with the flat of his sword, then again, and again, then stops to think.
question: After three strikes, how many boulders are rolling in the gorge?
solution: Strike two: each of the 4 becomes 4, so 4 x 4 = 16.
Strike three: 16 x 4 = 64 boulders — so Mr 6 sheathes his sword and rolls them into a stone bridge instead.
praise: Tracking the strikes one at a time is the right method — each strike multiplies the whole pile by 4, it doesn't just add 4 more.
hint: Write the count after each strike: 1, then 4, then... does the pile grow by adding 4 or by multiplying by 4?
victory: Mr 6 lines the 64 boulders up into a tidy staircase and walks the shepherds out over Knurlvex's own head. "Thanks for the building materials," he says politely.
imagePrompt: A cracked granite boulder-beast with glowing seams multiplying into dozens of rolling stones in a dusty canyon, a numeral-six knight standing calmly with his sword sheathed as sunlight beams through the gorge.
